clue.text: Given to stealing, as Bunter often was

definitions.meaning: a thief is said to have light, grasping fingers that things cling to
Billy Bunter, the greedy fat schoolboy of British comic fiction, usually had hands smeared with jam and sweets

explanation.surface: A remark that the famously greedy schoolboy Bunter had a habit of pilfering.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a gluttonous schoolboy from Frank Richards' Greyfriars stories, forever eating cakes and tuck, so his fingers were literally sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone light-fingered who pockets things is idiomatically described this way, as is anyone with jammy hands.

clue.text: Where philatelists gather?

parts.note: a favourite haunt is jokingly read as a place where stamp collectors meet to deal in stamps

explanation.surface: A question about the meeting place of stamp collectors.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a regular haunt, punningly taken literally as a place for stamps.

clue.text: Temporary home — perhaps Hilary secures one

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the term holds the next piece fast within it

parts.note: Hilary is a university term at Oxford, so an example of a term
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone named Hilary finds a stopgap place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hilary' looks like a person's name, but it is the spring term at Oxford and Dublin universities; 'secures' puts I inside TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something interim is provisional, lasting only until a permanent arrangement replaces it.

clue.text: Greek character one's employed in a bottling plant, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the worker's job title is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.words: one's employed in a bottling plant
parts.note: a capper is a worker or machine that puts caps on bottles

explanation.surface: A Greek person has a job at a bottling factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth letter of the Greek alphabet, and character means letter.

clue.text: Girl's happy event

definitions.meaning: a fortunate occurrence or piece of good luck

explanation.surface: A young woman's joyful occasion, such as a birth or wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is both a female first name and a word for happiness or a fortunate happening.

clue.text: Étude — it is mixed in a room in a recording studio

definitions.text: a room in a recording studio

indicators.note: the letters of the musical piece and the two short words are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A piano study gets mixed down in a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' suits a recording studio, but here it rearranges ETUDE and IT IS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An edit suite is a studio room fitted with equipment for editing sound or video recordings.

clue.text: Parking available in fine city over big stores

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the whole assembly is read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI

indicators.note: the parking letter is found within the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
P is the map abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Car parking is on offer at a grand city's large shops.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is written with the letter I standing in for the figure 1; in a down clue 'over' turns the whole build upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large shop or trading centre.

clue.text: Be off then on? Damn both the taps!

parts.note: blow is a mild curse, as in 'blow it!'
a basin has a hot tap and a cold tap

explanation.surface: Someone cursing a shower that keeps cutting out, swearing at both taps.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow hot and cold is an idiom for vacillating, keen one moment and cool the next.

clue.text: Device in aircraft lit up too, alarmingly, after start of ascent

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come after that opening letter
takes just the opening letter of the following word
something done alarmingly is done in a disturbing, disordered way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning light comes on in a plane as it begins to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarmingly' looks like it describes the warning light, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot is the system that flies an aircraft automatically, keeping its course without the pilot.

clue.text: One representative the Spanish push forward

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A single Spanish delegate is urging something onward.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge something onward, a direct synonym of propel.

clue.text: Windproof jacket used by old man protecting chest

indicators.note: the father's letters wrap round the box, shielding it

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Dad keeps his anorak on to keep his chest warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' looks anatomical, which suits the jacket, but it is a box, ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded weatherproof coat originally from the Arctic.

clue.text: Twist county's oarsmen

parts.note: Cork is a county in Ireland; the possessive gives the S
a crew is the team of rowers in a boat

explanation.surface: A provincial rowing team takes a sharp turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is a spiral, and as a verb it means to twist or move in a spiral.

clue.text: Able to calculate true mean in a different way

indicators.note: the words are to be set down with their letters in some other order

explanation.surface: A remark that an average can be worked out by another method.
explanation.definitionFit: Being numerate means having basic competence with numbers, the arithmetic counterpart of literate.

clue.text: Hint about a rest

indicators.note: the prompt goes round the single letter

parts.note: a reminder is a prompt or nudge, a hint

explanation.surface: A gentle suggestion about having a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest of something.

clue.text: Dominating woman in house hiding key

indicators.note: the sign conceals the musical key within it

parts.note: Virgo is one of the twelve astrological houses or signs
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A bossy woman at home has hidden the door key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' and 'key' suggest a home, but the house is an astrological sign and the key a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, aggressive woman, a shrew or harridan.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly heartily burrowing into vegetable bed, moving about

indicators.note: the bug's heart digs into the root vegetable, ending up inside it

parts.note: a carrot is a root vegetable

indicators.note: takes only the central letters, the heart, of the bug's name

explanation.surface: A bug tunnels into a vegetable patch and wriggles around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' looks like a garden bed for the vegetable, but with 'moving about' it defines a portable bed; 'heartily' gives YC, the middle of CREEPYCRAWLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrycot is a small portable bed for a baby, carried about by handles.

clue.text: Good butter, extremely milky, gets award

parts.note: a ram is an animal that butts, a butter

indicators.note: takes the letters at the extremes, first and last, of the word

explanation.surface: Good dairy butter, very creamy, wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' looks like the dairy spread but is one who butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grammy is an annual American award for achievement in the music industry.

clue.text: Intricately traced round in style of interior design

indicators.note: done intricately, the letters are worked into an elaborate new pattern

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A pattern elaborately traced in a circle in a decorator's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s, much used in interiors.

clue.text: Canal I've diverted to Spanish port

indicators.note: a diverted waterway has been turned from its course, so the letters are rerouted

explanation.surface: Someone has rerouted a waterway to reach a harbour in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a Mediterranean seaport city on the east coast of Spain.

clue.text: Short job adding one flipping ounce of sausage

indicators.note: the word for a task is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a chore is a routine job
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, the abbreviation is turned over, read upwards

explanation.surface: A quick task involves weighing out a small amount of sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorizo is a spicy Spanish pork sausage flavoured with paprika.

clue.text: Walk out with coin

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to stamp or mint a coin or medal

explanation.surface: Someone leaving with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a walkout by workers, and to strike a coin is to mint it.

clue.text: Not possible to get better suiting, from him?

parts.note: out means ruled out, as in 'that option is out'
fitter means in better condition, healthier

explanation.surface: A tailor's boast that no one could find a better suit anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: an outfitter is the person you would get suiting from.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or tailor supplying clothes, so a source of suits.

clue.text: Keen to employ old dodge

indicators.note: the eager word takes on, holds within it, the abbreviation

parts.note: avid means eager, keen

explanation.surface: An eager person uses an old trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to dodge or evade it.

clue.text: Foreman losing head in rage

indicators.note: the word for a work-gang boss drops its first letter

parts.note: a ganger is the foreman of a gang of labourers

explanation.surface: A works supervisor flies off the handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is intense displeasure, and rage is its extreme form.

clue.text: Very much ungoverned, oddly defective

indicators.note: the word is missing its odd-numbered letters, leaving only the even ones

explanation.surface: An unruly system is strangely faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: No end is an informal idiom meaning greatly or immensely, as in 'it pleased me no end'.

clue.text: On the sly, poured out gin and tonic, nothing more

indicators.note: the drink's letters are tipped out and mixed into a new order

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A drinker pours a gin and tonic and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' between the drinks is only a link, not fodder, and 'more' joins on the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito means in disguise, with identity concealed, so done secretly.

clue.text: Rude? It certainly is

parts.note: the word rude has four letters, and an obscene swear word is itself rude

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether a remark is rude replies that it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a swear word, and the word rude itself happens to be one in length.
